tasks.gr11-price-elasticity-t2: Topic: Price elasticity of demand and supply. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover PED = %ΔQd / %ΔP and PES = %ΔQs / %ΔP, interpretation of elastic (|e|>1), inelastic (|e|<1) and unit elastic (|e|=1) results. Factors affecting PED: availability of substitutes, necessity vs luxury, proportion of income, time period. Factors affecting PES: time period, spare capacity, stock levels, factor mobility. Include the total revenue test for PED, graph interpretation, and applications to taxation of inelastic goods.
tasks.gr11-income-cross-elasticity-t2: Topic: Income and cross elasticity of demand. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover YED = %ΔQd / %ΔY: positive YED = normal good, negative YED = inferior good; XED = %ΔQd(A) / %ΔP(B): positive = substitutes, negative = complements. Apply to SA consumer behaviour — how income shocks and rising fuel prices affect demand for related goods. Include formula calculations, graph interpretation, and case study analysis.
tasks.gr11-market-structures-t2: Topic: Market structures, costs and revenue. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover the four market structures: perfect competition (many sellers, identical product, price takers), monopolistic competition (many sellers, differentiated products), oligopoly (few large firms, interdependence, price leadership), monopoly (single seller, barriers to entry). Also cover fixed, variable, total, average and marginal costs; total and marginal revenue; profit maximisation at MC=MR. Include SA industry examples and graph interpretation.
tasks.gr11-gini-redistribution-t2: Topic: Gini coefficient and income redistribution. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover the Lorenz curve (plotting cumulative income share against cumulative population), Gini coefficient (area between Lorenz and line of equality divided by total triangle area, range 0–1), SA's Gini coefficient of approximately 0.63 as one of the world's highest. Redistribution policies: progressive income tax, VAT zero-rating, social grants (child support, old age, disability), Broad-Based BEE, land reform. Evaluate effectiveness with data.
tasks.gr11-economic-growth-wealth-t2: Topic: Wealth creation and economic growth (Grade 11 Economics, Term 2). Cover the wealth creation process (production, income, saving and investment), economic growth as growth of real GDP, growth rate = (later GDP − earlier GDP) ÷ earlier GDP × 100, real GDP = nominal GDP ÷ price index × 100, GDP per capita, methods of raising growth (investment, skills, technology, trade, stable policy), constraints on growth (skills shortage, electricity, transport, low saving, uncertainty, unemployment), South Africa's recent growth experience described qualitatively as low and uneven, and the standard of living. Use imaginary figures and give them in the question; do not quote real South African growth rates. Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate and explain.
tasks.gr11-marginal-utility-t2: Topic: Marginal utility (Grade 11 Economics, Term 2). Cover utility, total utility (the running total of marginal utilities), marginal utility (the change in total utility from one more unit), the law of diminishing marginal utility, total utility at its maximum where marginal utility is zero, consumer equilibrium (equal marginal utility per rand for all goods bought and the budget spent) and the link to the downward-sloping demand curve. Give the utility schedules in the question. Ask Grade 11 learners to compute total and marginal utility and to find the best purchase.
